QIMING / UPDATES

Changelog

What changed, which problems it addresses, how to use it, and what remains unverified.

2026-10-24

v0.3.0 · Know your version and resume existing work

This release addresses several concrete problems: not knowing which version a project uses, scattering one task across chats, mistaking an entry refresh for a review of every record, and using a parent project’s identity inside an independent child project.

Added: version reporting and official update checks

Downloading a new package does not update the instance inside an existing project. version reports both versions, source commits and instance identity. check-update queries official GitHub releases. Network failures, rate limits and unrecognized versions return an unknown outcome. Checking does not download software or overwrite the project.

Check this project’s Qiming instance version, the package version, and available official updates. Do not upgrade yet.

Merged: reuse task conversations and leave a handoff before splitting

Merged the conversation rules contributed from another device. For example, when a site edit leads to deployment work, look for an existing conversation for that task first. When a split is needed, verify project and working-directory identity, then retain outcomes, verification and next steps before completion or archiving. The current helper targets Codex conversation APIs and returns recommendations only; creating conversations, messaging and archiving still depend on host capabilities and user authorization.

Apply this project’s Qiming conversation rules to this task. Look for a reusable conversation first. If a split is needed, record outcomes, verification and next steps, then verify the new conversation’s project and working directory.

Corrected: report what an entry refresh actually checked

refresh_context now distinguishes a refreshed generated entry block from an unchecked short entry, linked tasks and summary accuracy. If a finished task still appears as in progress in START.md, refreshing AGENTS.md alone will not correct it. Task records and startup summaries need separate review when work ends.

Fixed: respect independent child-project boundaries

The conversation helper now uses shared project-boundary checks. An independent .git or .qiming entry in a child directory prevents it from borrowing the parent identity. The Agent must switch to the child project’s own instance. Code references between projects do not merge their management scopes.

How existing users upgrade

Run upgrade_preview from the new package, inspect local changes, then upgrade unchanged resources. We tested 0.2.2 discovering 0.3.0 and retaining edited rules, existing tasks, layout and instance identity; logging and search still worked afterward. Keep .qiming and do not reinitialize over an existing project.

Read this project’s START.md first. Use the new official package to run upgrade_preview and list incoming changes and local edits. Preserve my rules, directories, tasks and member IDs, then upgrade unchanged resources. Check versions, search, log append and host bindings afterward.

What has been verified

v0.3.0 is a preview release. All 248 local tests, 233 standalone public-package tests and six Linux/macOS CI jobs passed. Three Windows configurations remain unverified: the bounded diagnostic timed out without usable logs, so the cause is unknown. Public npx installation, customized old-instance upgrades, four-language site resources and desktop/mobile layouts were checked. The complete real-Agent behavior matrix has not been run.

GitHub release notes and downloads

2026-10-03

v0.2.2 · Existing folders and explicit onboarding

Clarified record path bases and skipped-file coverage; added optional category filters, root entry selection and preview, four English operating guides, and security/infrastructure references.

2026-10-01

v0.2.1 · Local edits and onboarding polish

Local edits now produce traceable warnings; missing files still fail. Successful operations clean their own staging. Source provenance, package fingerprints and init summaries are clearer; quick logging defaults to the selected work ID.

2026-10-01

v0.2.0 · Onboarding and recovery fixes

Added init, project bindings, safe upgrade previews and stale-lock inspection. Recursive JSON records support search and quick logging; improved credential checks and ordinary URL handling. Published automated tests and a three-OS CI matrix. Check Actions for results; the complete agent behavior matrix is still pending.

2026.10.01

Six focused field guides replace one long article

The original guide is now a six-part series covering the overview, local AI, a Pi child member, delivery boundaries, research and operations, and site release. The old URL remains; each article states the problem, actions, artifacts, and verification limits.

2026.10.01

Article layout and cache fix

Article headings, borders, reading width, and the mobile contents menu now follow one layout. CSS and JavaScript URLs change with their content to avoid stale styles.

2026.10.01

A dedicated Articles section

All four home and how-it-works pages state fit and limits in plain language. The new Articles section links to a Simplified Chinese field guide on local AI management and sanitized project cases.

2026.10.01

Topic pages and quick logging

The site now has separate topic pages in four languages and a sanitized OpenCode field report. The Skill adds controlled quick logging; a complete OpenCode replay remains pending.

2026.09.28

Official domain and search access

The official site moved to qiming.dashen.wang with direct Cloudflare Pages hosting and proxying enabled. All four language pages include search metadata, a sitemap, and visible FAQs.

2026.09.28

Project scope and continuity

Improved project-owned instances, startup context, agent instructions, and ownership of derived capabilities. Evidence records 112 automated checks and a targeted Codex trial; the full cross-agent matrix remains untested.

2026.09.27

A usable management seed

Established the Skill entry, deterministic tools, source mapping, member and knowledge records, export, and recovery rehearsal.
